findings.title: Costs
findings.text: Slippage and commissions cost 0.052R per trade on average (+0.342R before costs, +0.290R after). Costs are affordable here.

findings.title: Win rate vs what's needed
findings.text: Win rate 25.7% against about 21.1% needed to break even with the actual average winner (+5.00R) and loser (-1.33R). Median target was 2.0R; only 29.7% of trades ever reached +2R before exiting.

findings.title: False breakouts
findings.text: 75.5% of stopped trades were stopped within 2 bars of entry: the move reversed almost immediately. That is a lot of instant failures, typical of breakouts in choppy markets.

findings.title: Giving back winners
findings.text: 5.5% of losing trades were up at least +1R at some point before turning into a loss. Few losers were ever meaningfully profitable, so exit management isn't the main problem.

findings.title: Stop placement
findings.text: 0.0% of stopped trades went on to reach the original target later the same day. Wider stops mean smaller positions, so this is a trade-off to test, not a fix.

findings.title: Long vs short
findings.text: Best: long +0.820R over 35 trades (95% interval [-1.023, 3.083]). Worst: short -0.185R over 39 trades (interval [-0.952, 0.399]).

findings.title: Setups with positive evidence
findings.text: None. No setup or ticker slice has an out-of-sample 95% interval entirely above zero.

diagnostics.caveat: These slices describe past out-of-sample trades. Choosing filters from them and re-testing on the same trades would be curve-fitting; any idea here must be confirmed on later data.

search.note: Each fold tried 1 parameter combinations on its training window and kept the best. The more combinations tried, the more the training winner is a lucky draw - which is exactly why only the following, unseen test window is reported.
